'''Isabelle M. Côté''' is a professor of [[marine ecology]] at [[Simon Fraser University]] in Canada.

==Life and education==
Côté is from [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]]. She received her [[B.Sc.]] in [[marine biology]] from [[McGill University]] in 1984, her [[M.Sc.]] in [[zoology]] from the [[University of Alberta]] in 1987,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cote |first=Isabelle Marie |date=1987 |title=Mate choice and spawning periodicity in the redlip blenny (Pisces:Blenniidae) |url=https://era.library.ualberta.ca/items/edb08b2c-1288-4500-b1d3-e82371abc708 |access-date=2024-02-18 |website=ERA |language=en |doi=10.7939/r3t727s0p}}</ref> and her [[Ph.D.]] in behavioral ecology from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1993. In 2023 she was elected as a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-05 |title=The RSC Presents the Class of 2023 |url=https://rsc-src.ca/en/news/press-release-rsc-presents-class-2023 | access-date=2024-02-18 |website=Royal Society of Canada |language=en }}</ref> Her research is notable for its impact on [[coral reef]] conservation.

==Career==
Côté pioneered the use of [[meta-analyses]] in marine conservation. Her research has addressed the extent of coral reef declines in the Caribbean at a regional level,<ref name="Gardneretal">{{Cite journal |last1=Gardner|first1=T.A. |last2=Côté |first2= I.M. |last3= Gill |first3 = J.A. |last4= Grant |first4 = A |last5=Watkinson |first5=A.R. |year = 2003 |title = Long term region-wide declines in Caribbean corals |journal=Science|issue= 5635 |pages = 958–960 |doi=10.1126/science.1086050 |volume=301 |pmid=12869698|bibcode=2003Sci...301..958G |s2cid=42807853 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and measured the effectiveness of [[marine protected areas]] at enhancing fish and their habitats. Côté and coauthors demonstrated that protected areas were not necessarily more resistant to [[climate change]].<ref name="Darlingetal">{{Cite journal |last1=Darling|first1=E.R. |last2=McClanahan |first2= T.R. |last3= Côté |first3 = I.M.|year = 2010 |title = Combined effects of two stressors on Kenyan coral reefs are additive or antagonistic, not synergistic |journal=Conservation Letters|volume= 3 |issue=2 |pages = 122–130 |doi= 10.1111/j.1755-263X.2009.00089.x|s2cid=28112526 |doi-access= free |bibcode=2010ConL....3..122D }}</ref><ref name="Darling&Cote">{{Cite journal |last1=Darling|first1=E.R. |last2= Côté |first2 = I.M.|year = 2010 |title = Rethinking ecosystem resilience in the face of climate change |journal=PLOS Biology|volume= 8|issue=7 |article-number = e1000438 |doi= 10.1371/journal.pbio.1000438|pmid=20668536 |pmc=2910654 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Her recent research has focused on the dramatic invasion of Indo-Pacific [[lionfish]] throughout the Caribbean, with a focus on [[Subtidal|sub-tidal]] research.<ref name="Greenetal">{{Cite journal |last1=Green|first1=S.J. |last2=Tamburello |first2= N. |last3= Miller |first3 = S.E. |last4= Akins |first4 = J.L. |last5=Côté |first5=I.M. |year = 2014 |title = Habitat complexity and fish size affect the detection of Indo-Pacific lionfish on invaded coral reefs |journal=Coral Reefs|volume= 32 |issue=2 |pages = 413–421 |doi=10.1007/s00338-012-0987-8|s2cid=14111741 }}</ref><ref name="Greenetal2">{{Cite journal |last1= Green|first1=S.J. |last2=Dulvy |first2=N.K.|last3=Brooks |first3=A.L.M. |last4=Akins |first4 = J.L. |last5=Cooper |first5=AB |last6=Miller |first6 = S |last7=Côté |first7=I.M. |year=2014 |title = Linking removal targets to the ecological effects of invaders: a predictive model and field test |journal = Ecological Applications |doi=10.1890/13-0979.1 |volume=24 |issue=6 |pages=1311–1322|pmid=29160656 |bibcode=2014EcoAp..24.1311G |url=https://ir.library.oregonstate.edu/downloads/s4655h76p}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Levine|first=Alaina G.|date=2020-09-17|title=Planning beyond the pandemic: Faculty career development in the age of COVID-19|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/planning-beyond-pandemic-faculty-career-development-age-covid-19|access-date=2021-07-08|website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en}}</ref>

Previously, she was a faculty member at the [[University of East Anglia]] in Norwich, UK.

Côté has published over 200 academic publications on [[behavioural ecology]], [[coral reef ecology]], and [[conservation biology|conservation]], receiving over 20,000 citations, resulting in an [[h-index]] and [[i10-index]] of 67 and 200 respectively.<ref name="Google Scholar">{{cite web|date=|title=Isabelle Côté - Google Scholar Citations|url=https://scholar.google.ca/citations?user=_8OMcbUAAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=2014-11-09|publisher=Scholar.google.ca}}</ref> Côté has spoken about different aspects of marine conservation for different media outlets, including [[CBC News]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Shepherd|first=Jenni|date=May 22, 2014|title=Shipwrecked camera found underwater after 2 years with photos intact|work=CBC News|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/shipwrecked-camera-found-underwater-after-2-years-with-photos-intact-1.2651173}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* Murray A. Newman Award for significant contributions to advancing conservation and research efforts in BC and beyond (2008)<ref>{{cite web |title=Coté wins Newman award for ocean conservation and research |url=https://www.sfu.ca/science/news-events/news/2018/cote-wins-newman-award-for-ocean-conservation-and-research.html |website=Simon Frasier University |access-date=26 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130233609/https://www.sfu.ca/science/news-events/news/2018/cote-wins-newman-award-for-ocean-conservation-and-research.html |archive-date=30 November 2020 |date=24 April 2018}}</ref>
* Leopold Leadership Fellows by Stanford University's Stanford Woods Institute for the Environment (2015)
* [[Marsh Award for Conservation Biology]] by the [[Zoological Society of London]]  for "contributions of fundamental science to the conservation of animal species and habitats" (2008)<ref name="MarshAward">{{citation|title=Marsh Award for Conservation Biology - Isabelle Côté|url=http://www.marshchristiantrust.org/IsabelleC%C3%B4t%C3%A9|access-date=2014-11-10|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141110025147/http://www.marshchristiantrust.org/IsabelleC%C3%B4t%C3%A9|archive-date=2014-11-10|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

* 2016. JA Schultz, RN Cloutier, IM Côté. "Evidence for a trophic cascade on rocky reefs following sea star mass mortality in British Columbia". ''[[PeerJ]]'' 4, e1980
*2019. BR Howard, FT Francis, IM Côté, TW Therriault. "Habitat alteration by invasive European green crab (''Carcinus maenas)'' causes eelgrass loss in British Columbia, Canada". ''Biol Invasions'' 21, 3607-3618
